dataset.title: Expression data from Breast cancer subtypes
dataset.citation: Gruosso et al., EMBO Molecular Medicine 2016
dataset.processing: The data were first normalized by using GC-RMA (R version 2.14.1). A linear mixed model using Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML using name package) was then applied. The model included the different experimental batches and the sample type as fixed effects, and treated technical variation as random effects. No interaction terms were included. This model was used to derive significance for differential expression between different tumor types and for correction of batch and hybridization effects. For further analysis, technical replicates were averaged. We choose to discard probe-sets with noise-level signal from the analysis: specifically, we considered as not expressed and therefore discarded, all the probe-sets with a log2 intensity of less than 4 in 95% or more of tissue samples.

logDecision.reason: The maximum is below 20 and the median is about 6.6, which is the range of log2 GC-RMA output. The processing statement confirms GC-RMA.

summary.headline: Mostly cell division, but not only. Cell-division genes are the biggest theme (22 of the 50 strongest differences), and 21 of them classify the subtypes almost as well as all 28,592 probes (AUC 0.98 vs 0.99). A second line, the HER2 amplicon on chromosome 17, separates them just as well, and even with both removed the score is 0.96.

classifier.verdict: Proliferation genes alone reach AUC 0.98 against 0.99 for every probe (difference +0.01, corrected p = 0.33). Masking the whole proliferation programme still leaves 0.97, partly because the 17q12 HER2 amplicon separates the subtypes on its own (AUC 0.98, exploratory). With both lines masked the score is still 0.96; with shuffled labels it falls to 0.50, 0.56, so this is not leakage.

enrichment.method: One-sided hypergeometric test of every Gene Ontology biological process (10–500 genes) in the GPL570 annotation, run separately for the 3,106 genes higher in Luminal B and the 2,566 higher in Luminal A at FDR 5%, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction across processes.
